$description: No hue at all: ink on pure greys, crisp ruled lines, square 2px buttons and controls, 4px cards, Geist Mono headings over Geist.

accent.$description: Points at color.grey: the accent is ink, with no hue (design-system/tokens/primitives.tokens.json).

neutral.$description: Points at color.grey, zero chroma at every step (design-system/tokens/primitives.tokens.json).

radius.$description: The sharpest scale: 2px for chips, controls, buttons and menus, 4px cards, 6px panels and dialogs.
2px: square buttons with the same corner as the controls.

pull.$description: Geist Mono gives a comma or full stop a full-width cell, which leaves about 0.27em of air before the mark against 0.09em between letters. The pull takes out the difference, so a word-ending mark sits at the same gap as the letters before it.

decoration-line.$description: The accent is ink, so links and active items carry an underline at rest.

ring.$description: The accent point is ink like the tile, so a canvas-coloured ring keeps it visible.

heading.$description: Geist Mono at the heading roles' 800 and 700: a monospaced heading voice over Geist body copy.

type.$description: Tracking for Geist Mono at 800 and 700. Every glyph has the same cell, and wide letters such as m and w fill theirs, so the pull stops where a double m still keeps a hairline of air at hero size (about 0.005em) and eases off as the size drops.

brand.$description: Ink: links, active indicators and the highlighted word match the headings, and the underline at rest tells a link apart.

brand-subtle.$description: Without hue, a brand chip, tinted bubble or selection can only differ by lightness, so the quiet brand fill sits well below secondary (0.82 against 0.955 L): a Pro badge reads as a darker grey than a Draft badge, with ink text far above 4.5:1.

ring.$description: Mid graphite, not ink: it keeps 3:1 on the canvas (4.6:1) and on dark panels and their raised surfaces (4.1:1 and 3.8:1), where an ink ring would vanish.

border.$description: One step darker than the other themes: with no hue and no tint, ruled lines carry the structure, like the grid of a spec sheet. Still a 1px hairline.

border-strong.$description: Outline buttons, inputs and selected cards read as drawn boxes.

popover-border.$description: Menus and popovers float without a shadow or a tinted surface, so their edge matches the strong line.

tint.$description: Lightness is the only cue without hue. Neighbouring tints in this order (wrapping round) sit at least 0.04 L apart, and mint stays 0.055 L from secondary, the +N chip after an avatar stack. The strength order matches in both modes: rose, sand, violet, mint, sky (the lightest, for large tiles).

chart.$description: Lightness is the only cue, so the order is chosen for separation rather than as a ramp. The first three series, which charts use together most, take the ends and the middle of the usable range: ink, a mid grey (0.44) and the lightest grey that still holds 3:1 on white (0.66), so Jordan, Sam and Sofia stay about 0.22 L apart or more, even as 8px legend dots and 2px lines. Series 5 (Late, comparison baselines) sits between 3 and 2, well clear of ink, and series 4 between 1 and 3. Prominence runs 1, 4, 3, 5, 2 in both modes. Every series holds 3:1 on the canvas and on cards.

brand.$description: Near-white ink, as in light mode.

brand-subtle.$description: Well above secondary (0.36 against 0.215 L), for the same reason as in light mode.

border.$description: A step brighter than the other themes, for the same ruled-grid reason as in light mode.

tint.$description: Lightness is the only cue without hue. Neighbouring tints in this order (wrapping round) sit at least 0.04 L apart, and mint stays 0.055 L from secondary, the +N chip after an avatar stack. The strength order matches in both modes: rose, sand, violet, mint, sky (the lightest, for large tiles).

chart.$description: The light order mirrored, with the same prominence (1, 4, 3, 5, 2): near-white first, series 3 a light grey and series 2 the dimmest, about 0.2 L apart; 5 between 3 and 2, and 4 between 1 and 3. Series 2 to 4 also hold 4.5:1 on the terminal surface, because code blocks colour tags, strings and attributes with them, and attributes (series 4) no longer match the comment grey.
